summary_of_pdf: Formal notice of defensive publication and technical disclosure delivered via RPost by Reinaldo J. Aguiar Marcano to executives and outside counsel at major aerospace and satellite imaging corporations (Maxar, Airbus, Planet, BlackSky, Satellogic). The instrument asserts the establishment of definitive prior art in satellite vision systems and optical communications through a published 721-page portfolio of five USPTO patent applications. It further notices a perpetual, no-fee license granted to the U.S. Federal Government and includes highly adversarial attachments alleging criminal wire fraud and whistleblower retaliation.
attorneys_comments: This instrument functions as a highly aggressive, multi-pronged notice letter designed to establish evidentiary proof of delivery (via RPost) for both defensive publication (prior art under 35 U.S.C. § 102) and potential willful infringement claims (35 U.S.C. § 284). The sender's tactical deployment of a U.S. Government license implicates 28 U.S.C. § 1498, potentially shielding government contractors from direct infringement liability while preserving claims against commercial applications. The inclusion of 'Formal Criminal Referrals' for Interstate Wire Fraud and whistleblower documents introduces severe collateral liabilities and suggests a highly volatile, quasi-pro se litigant posture. Evidentiary strength is bolstered by the RPost delivery receipt, which will satisfy FRCP Rule 4 and 5 notice requirements for actual knowledge. Counsel must immediately quarantine the technical disclosures to prevent contamination of ongoing internal R&D, assess the cited USPTO applications for patentability, and evaluate the criminal referral attachments for potential SEC material risk disclosure obligations or ABA Model Rule 8.3 reporting duties.
recommended_next_steps: 1. Institute an immediate clean-room protocol and litigation hold regarding the cited USPTO applications to mitigate willful infringement risks. 2. Conduct a Freedom to Operate (FTO) analysis against the five enumerated USPTO applications. 3. Review the attached 'Criminal Referral' documents to determine if any internal investigations or SEC disclosures are warranted. 4. Verify the EPO NPL indexing and USPTO prosecution status of the cited applications. 5. Do not respond directly to the sender; route all communications through outside IP litigation counsel.
